key_insight: The 2D/3D perovskite band alignment is highly sensitive to surface termination and chemical composition, meaning interface chemistry can strongly reshape device energetics.
engineering_relevance: Controlling 2D passivation layers and 3D surface chemistry could help tune band offsets, reduce interfacial losses, and improve perovskite solar-cell stability and performance.
method: Hybrid first-principles simulations with hybrid functionals
Atomistic modeling of (PEA)2PbI4 / mixed-cation mixed-halide 3D perovskite interfaces
Consistent calculation of work function, electron affinity, and band offsets across terminations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports termination-dependent work functions and band offsets, with valence band offsets ranging from 0.2 to 0.7 eV and conduction offsets around 0.25 eV.
watch_item: These are preliminary simulation results, so the predicted offsets may depend on the chosen surface cleavage, composition, and modeling assumptions before experimental validation.
paper_title: Material chemical composition impacts on the band alignments: preliminary results on the 3D/2D perovskite interfaces
